_comment: What red looks like on `main`. Keyed on file+name and never on the TAP
number, because `node --test` numbers the run flat and one new test file
703 pass, 4 fail, 0 skipped. The same four, and only those four, also fail
on ursa-exo/2026-11-02-message-7 (`1..473`, `# tests 759`) after a register
merge — which is both how that merge was proved to have broken nothing and
how the trunk was found red.
`minPoints` is a floor on TOP-LEVEL points (node's `1..N`), not on
`# tests`. Those are 421 and 707 here and conflating them refuses a
healthy suite; this seat did exactly that on the tool's first real run.
`owner` is established from an open row that touches the failing file, or
it says UNOWNED. It is never a guess about whose lane a file looks like.

red.name: transcribed: the events read refuses unknown filters, so the INERT finding was acted on
red.note: A tripwire on HQ's api.py, vendored locally. It fired because its subject moved, which is the job. Security's #709 touches this exact file and its title names a tripwire that called HQ's repair a regression, so this one is owned and in flight. Not re-reported.

red.name: the shipped registry has no errors for the seat that owns the files it can fix
red.note: Two error-severity findings where the assertion wants none, and candidates 14 against sites 16: two probe-found candidates are not registered sites. The test's own message is 'the gate must be green on the branch that introduces it' — it is not green on main. No open row touches this file.

red.name: every real heading that announces a scan is classified as one
red.note: Asserts on live docs/ideas.md content. No open row touches this file; seven open rows append to docs/ideas.md.

red.name: the real file has exactly one tag-announced scan, and it is the one measured
red.note: Expected 1, got 0. The test matches a heading spelled `### 2026-11-02 (engineer, craft scan) —`; docs/ideas.md now spells it `### 2026-11-02 (engineer, message run) — Craft scan: ...`, with the scan word moved past the em dash. The test's own comment anticipated the count RISING ('a second one appearing here is a reason to re-read the rule') and has no reading for it falling to zero. The convention moved; the assertion did not.
